---
title: "Maintain the Schema"
---

The schema is edited as CSV files, checked against a data dictionary by the `data-dict` command-line tool, and stored as Parquet. You edit two kinds of file; the rest are generated or only read. The table layouts are described in the [schema reference](../reference/schema.qmd).

## Which files to touch

| File | What you do with it |
|---|---|
| `schema/*.csv` | Edit. This is the content: categories, datasets, the crosswalk, the dictionary registry, and the drift log. Separate multiple values in one cell with semicolons (for example `CO2;CH4`). Leave a cell empty when there is no value; do not use a dash as a placeholder. |
| `schema/data-dict.yaml` | Edit only when the structure changes: a new column, a new allowed value, or a new rule. Record unfinished work as a `todo:` entry so the tool reports it on every run. |
| `R/build_schema_parquet.R` | Run after any edit. Do not edit unless a column is added or removed. |
| `R/ghgi_schema.R` | Use for queries; see [Query the schema](query-the-schema.qmd). |
| `schema/parquet/` | Generated by the build script. Never edit. |
| `docs/` | Generated by `quarto render`. Never edit; see [Render the documents](render-the-documents.qmd). The exception is `docs/schema-dictionary.html`, which the build script generates. |

## Build and validate

After editing any CSV file, run:

```r
source(here::here("R", "build_schema_parquet.R"))
```

This rebuilds the Parquet files and validates them at three levels: the dictionary itself, the column names and types, and the values. If any check fails, the script stops and the message names the rule and the rows that broke it. Fix the CSV file, or the rule if the rule is wrong, and run it again. Warnings about unresolved `todo` entries are reminders, not failures.

When every check passes, the script also regenerates `docs/schema-dictionary.html`, a browsable page of the dictionary for colleagues who don't use R or Git. It is a single file that opens in any browser, so copy it to the shared drive after each rebuild.

The script needs the `data-dict` command-line tool, version 0.0.3, either on your `PATH` or in `~/bin` (`C:\Users\<you>\bin` on Windows). Install the prebuilt binary from the [`tidyverse/data-dict` releases](https://github.com/tidyverse/data-dict/releases/tag/v0.0.3) (on Windows, `data-dict-cli-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`) and check it against its `.sha256` file. Do not build it from source.

## Adding a new dataset

1. Add a row to `ghgi_datasets.csv`, and link it to the categories that use it in `ghgi_category_datasets.csv`.
2. Run the build.
3. Run `dataset_home(schema)` to see where the dataset belongs: a sector's name means that sector's repository, and `shared` means the shared-data repository.
4. In that repository, once the cleaned table exists, add it to the repository's `data-dict.yaml`. The `r-data-dict-builder` custom AI tool can draft the entry.
5. Validate that dictionary with `data-dict validate-data <folder>`.
6. Register the dictionary in `ghgi_dictionaries.csv`, set the dataset's `dict_id` to it, and run the build again.
